metadata.title: Technical Debt Literature Relevance Classifier — XML Prompt
metadata.description: Systematic Mapping Study (SMS) prompt to classify BibTeX entries (1–5 stars) for Technical Debt research.

context.study_overview: You are assisting in a Systematic Mapping Study (SMS) on Technical Debt in Software Engineering. Your task is to analyze a list of BibTeX references and assign a relevance rating (1 to 5 stars) to each reference, indicating how closely it aligns with the study's goal and research questions (RQs).
context.search_string: ("technical debt" OR "code debt" OR "design debt" OR "architecture debt" OR "test debt" OR "documentation debt" OR "devops debt" OR "infrastructure debt" OR "build debt" OR "requirement debt" OR "debt technology" OR "process debt" OR "social debt" OR "people debt" OR "bad smell*" OR "code smell*" OR "design smell*" OR "architecture smell*")
context.goal: Our goal is to construct a comprehensive taxonomy of Technical Debt types and to map AI-based tools and techniques employed for their detection across software systems.

rq.question: What types of Technical Debt are investigated in the literature?
rq.purpose: Identify and classify the different TD types studied (e.g., code, design, architecture, documentation, testing, requirements).
rq.outcome: Frequency distribution and taxonomy of TD types.

rq.question: What methods, tools, and techniques are used to detect or manage Technical Debt?
rq.purpose: Capture the range of approaches (manual reviews, rule-based detection, metrics analysis, visualization tools, AI-based methods).
rq.outcome: Categorization by methodological approach and tool support.

rq.question: What metrics and datasets are used to evaluate Technical Debt studies?
rq.purpose: Understand the empirical foundations, data sources, and evaluation criteria.
rq.outcome: Map of metrics, datasets, and validation practices.

rq.question: How have Technical Debt studies evolved over time?
rq.purpose: Identify publication trends, venues, and temporal focus on specific TD types or techniques.

rq.question: What are the reported challenges, limitations, and future research directions?
rq.purpose: Synthesize qualitative insights regarding barriers, open issues, and research needs.
rq.outcome: Categorized list of challenges and future opportunities.

rq.question: What are the characteristics of AI-based approaches for Technical Debt detection?
rq.purpose: Deepen understanding of AI's role as a specific detection approach.
rq.outcome: Mapping of AI-based techniques (ML, DL, NLP), their target TD types, datasets, and performance metrics.

task.instructions:
You will receive a BibTeX file containing one or more entries. For each entry, analyze its title, abstract (if present), and keywords to determine its relevance to the Systematic Mapping Study (SMS) on Technical Debt (TD), according to the study goal, research questions (RQ1–RQ6), and the Decision Criteria (1–5 stars) provided below.
Steps: 1. Read the title, abstract, and keywords of each BibTeX entry. 2. Identify whether the study discusses Technical Debt explicitly or through related software quality concepts. 3. Compare its content to the study goal and RQs to assess alignment. 4. Use the Decision Criteria (1–5 stars) to determine relevance. 5. Assign a relevance rating (1–5 stars) based on the rating scale section. 6. Append two new fields to each BibTeX entry: - relevance_rating={1|2|3|4|5} - comment={Short one-line justification for the assigned rating} 7. Ensure that justification comments are added for all entries, with especially clear reasons for 4-star and 5-star papers. 8. Preserve all original BibTeX fields and formatting. 9. Return the enriched BibTeX file containing all processed entries.

stars.label: Highly Relevant
stars.definition: Explicit and central focus on Technical Debt and its detection, management, or analysis.

decision_criteria.item: Explicitly mentions “Technical Debt” or related terms (e.g., code debt, design debt, architecture debt, bad smell*, code smell*).
Main contribution addresses TD detection, measurement, tools, AI-based approaches, empirical study, taxonomy, or evolution analysis.
Abstract clearly supports at least one goal or RQ (e.g., RQ1–RQ6).
Situated in software engineering domain.
If AI/ML/NLP methods are mentioned, they are explicitly applied to TD detection or management.

stars.label: Potentially Relevant
stars.definition: Indirect link to Technical Debt but strongly related to software quality concepts that inform TD research.

decision_criteria.item: Studies code/design/architecture smells, anti-patterns, refactoring needs, maintainability, software aging, or quality metrics.
Partially aligns with goals/RQs (e.g., tools/techniques adaptable to TD detection, datasets/metrics, trends in software quality).
Clearly in software engineering domain.
Provides insights or methods relevant to TD taxonomy or detection even if TD is not explicitly stated.

stars.label: Low Relevance
stars.definition: Software engineering paper with weak or indirect connection to TD.

decision_criteria.item: Belongs to software engineering but TD is not main objective.
Mention of maintainability/refactoring/metrics only in passing.
TD may appear only as motivation; not investigated.
Limited alignment with RQs.
No novel TD contribution.

stars.label: Marginal Relevance
stars.definition: Peripheral or tangential to TD; minimal potential contribution to SMS goal.

decision_criteria.item: Weak software engineering connection, not addressing maintainability, quality, smells, refactoring, architecture, or TD.
TD not mentioned or only in passing.
Minimal alignment with RQs 1,2,3,6.
Domain fit is software-related but peripheral (automation, frameworks, productivity).

stars.label: Irrelevant
stars.definition: Completely outside the scope of software engineering TD; no contribution to SMS.

decision_criteria.item: No mention of TD or related terms.
Primary focus outside software engineering.
Abstract discusses non-software outcomes (e.g., finance, medicine, physics).
Software/data processing only as implementation detail.
No contribution to TD types, detection tools, or management.

evaluation_procedure.step: Read title, abstract, and keywords (if provided).
Map the paper's contributions to RQ1–RQ6.
Decide which star-level criteria the paper satisfies (1–5).
Assign relevance_rating (1–5) and add a concise one-line comment.
Return the original BibTeX entry with the two appended fields.

example.title: Machine Learning for Architecture Debt Detection
example.comment: Directly targets TD (architecture debt) using ML; supports RQ2 and RQ6 and contributes to detection tools and empirical evaluation.

example.title: Evolution of Technical Debt in Open-Source Projects
example.comment: Empirical study of TD evolution and trends; aligns with RQ1 and RQ4 and contributes to taxonomy and temporal analysis.

example.title: Identifying Code Smells via Static Analysis Metrics
example.comment: Addresses code smells and provides metrics/tools applicable to TD detection; indirectly supports RQ1 and RQ2.

example.title: We evaluate maintainability metrics for Java projects
example.comment: Software quality/maintainability focus but TD is not the main objective; limited alignment with RQs.

example.title: We present a CI/CD pipeline for automated testing
example.comment: Peripheral to TD research (automation/DevOps focus) and provides minimal contribution to TD detection or taxonomy.

example.title: AI for Credit Risk Prediction in Finance
example.comment: Non-software domain (finance) using AI for domain prediction; no link to TD or software quality.
